tools.name: chief_forge_init
tools.description: Run the forge pre-flight for one task — tracking issue, task branch, draft pull request — before chief_delegate. Refused for a plan until its required advisor review resolves. For a plan, call it only on a chain head (a wave nothing precedes) that has no worker yet: a chain has one branch and one pull request, its later waves continue it with chief_delegate replaces:, and the pull request body lists every wave of the chain. Returns the values, or a script to run yourself when the server could not. The pull request body is the reviewer's whole brief: planned work carries the plan summary and wave contracts (planThreadId and wave); unplanned work must pass mission, successCriteria and constraints, the same text you will pass to chief_delegate.

title.description: The exact title this task will be delegated with.

base.description: Branch to cut from and target the pull request at. Omit for the project default; name one only to stack deliberately on an open pull request. Stack only when this work builds on that pull request's changes; independent work gets its own PR on the default base.

body.description: Short summary for the issue and pull request body.

planThreadId.description: For planned work: the planner thread the task's wave comes from. Give it with wave; the plan summary and the wave's contracts are added to the issue and pull request body.

wave.description: For planned work: the 1-based wave this task implements. Give it with planThreadId.

mission.description: Required without planThreadId (unplanned work): the same mission you will pass to chief_delegate. It goes into the pull request body, which is the reviewer's whole brief.

successCriteria.description: The same success criteria you will pass to chief_delegate, as text (one per line).

constraints.description: The same constraints you will pass to chief_delegate, as text (one per line).

tools.name: chief_delegate
tools.description: Delegate one clearly titled unit of implementation work to a visible worker in its own managed worktree. See kind for Designer work. verifyCommand goes into the worker's brief as its own check. One plan chain has one branch, pull request and worktree: a later wave of a chain needs replaces: the chain's latest worker, replaces: never crosses to another chain, a started chain is not delegated fresh again, and a replacement keeps its prior's prUrl. replaces: is refused after 2 consecutive request_changes on the task until a consult has given its advice (a ready or blocked report), and from 3 on unless userApprovedRound is set; the count follows the replaces: chain and every reviewer, and only an approve resets it. A plan with more than one wave or marked complex is refused until its one advisor review resolves (chief_consult planThreadId).

title.description: Exact concise title for the worker thread. Optional: defaults to the first line of mission, clipped to 160 characters.

mission.description: What to achieve, in the user's terms. State a cause only when evidence already states it (see the core rules), naming its source; never your own guess.

successCriteria.description: Observable outcomes: each one checked by a command with its exit status, or named for Manual Verification.

constraints.description: Limits the work must respect: scope, files or behaviour to leave alone, user rules.

context.description: Supporting evidence, each item with its source (user message, issue, report, alert, reviewer verdict), plus links and prior work.

branch.description: The task branch Chief already created and pushed. The worktree is based on it and the worker commits there. Omit to base the worktree on the project default.

issueUrl.description: URL of the tracking issue Chief opened for this task, when the forge has issues.

prUrl.description: URL of the draft pull request Chief opened from the task branch. The worker never marks it ready.

replaces.description: A finished worker's thread id to hand off from: the new worker starts in that worker's worktree and branch, gets its latest review findings and the path to the reviewer's full verdict file, and the old worker is marked complete.

planThreadId.description: A planner thread that reported a wave schedule. Combined with wave, the plugin takes the plan file from that schedule.

unplannedReason.description: Required when planning is on and this work skips chief_plan: your reason for skipping the plan (your judgment; see the core rules). Not needed with planThreadId/wave or replaces.

kind.description: designer when the agent decides or implements how the UI looks: drawing or editing in a design tool (Paper, Figma, …), implementing a design-tool artboard in code (design-to-code), or building UI with no approved design or explicit visual spec. worker (the default) only when an approved design or an explicit spec in the request, an issue, or a report already fixes the look. A replaces: successor keeps the prior worker's kind. Exception: a plan's design-only wave (design: true) defaults to designer and only draws; the wave that implements its approved artboards is a worker. tester writes and runs tests, nothing else: a plan's test wave (test: true) defaults to tester on its first hand-off; on unplanned work it needs replaces:. Replacing a tester, or a worker on a test wave, needs an explicit kind: worker to change product code, tester to change tests. spec-writer changes docs/ only: a plan's spec: true implementation wave defaults to spec-writer on its first hand-off (its worker then replaces it with kind: worker); on a spec-bearing chain it also replaces the latest worker, designer or tester of a wave to fix the docs; on unplanned work it is opt-in, with or without replaces:.

userApprovedRound.description: Set only with replaces: and only after the user explicitly approved another review round in this thread: a replaced worker whose reviewer has requested changes 3 times in a row is refused without it.

verifyCommand.description: One shell command the worker's brief tells it to run after its last commit and get exit 0 from before reporting ready: a build/lint check for a worker, e.g. `npx tsc --noEmit && bb plugin build`; a tester's may be a filtered test command. Nothing reruns it: reviewers read code only. Inherited through replaces:.

tools.name: chief_plan
tools.description: Send one unit of work to a read-only planner. It proposes an implementation plan, split into waves; its ready alert names the exact next call. With revises, a fresh planner revises a plan whose one advisor review asked for changes; the revision is delegated with no second review.

title.description: Exact concise title for the worker thread. Optional: defaults to the first line of mission, clipped to 160 characters.

mission.description: What to achieve, in the user's terms. State a cause only when evidence already states it (see the core rules), naming its source; never your own guess.

context.description: Supporting evidence, each item with its source (user message, issue, report, alert, reviewer verdict), plus links and prior work.

revises.description: A planner whose plan its one advisor review sent back with changes: the new planner revises that plan with the advice attached, and its plan is delegated with no second review.

tools.name: chief_spawn
tools.description: Hand one task to a new Chief for this project when the user asks to do it in a new Chief. Pass a literal title, the user's request verbatim, and the context it needs (goal, evidence, linked threads, issues, PRs, branches, plan and verdict files, open decisions). todoId moves your own open todo to it. It never takes over your managed threads: hand over only a task with no unfinished worker — every worker on it complete (chief_stop and a ready report do not release a worker's branch); otherwise keep the task.

title.description: A literal task label, used in the new Chief's thread title. Optional: defaults to the first line of request, clipped to 160 characters.

request.description: The owner's words asking for this task, verbatim.

context.description: Goal and success criteria, evidence, linked threads/issues/PRs/branches, plan and verdict file paths, and open decisions.

todoId.description: Your own open todo to move to the new Chief.

tools.name: chief_consult
tools.description: Start a read-only advisor on a hard problem or a change that keeps failing review. It may read code and run commands to reproduce it, never edits, and reports its advice back to you. With planThreadId, it gives a multi-wave or complex plan its one review before delegation; refused for any other plan.

title.description: Exact concise title for the worker thread. Optional: defaults to the first line of mission, clipped to 160 characters.

mission.description: What to achieve, in the user's terms. State a cause only when evidence already states it (see the core rules), naming its source; never your own guess.

context.description: Supporting evidence, each item with its source (user message, issue, report, alert, reviewer verdict), plus links and prior work.

workerThreadId.description: The managed worker whose change keeps failing review: the advisor runs in its worktree and gets its brief, reviewer verdicts, and branch.

planThreadId.description: A planner whose multi-wave or complex plan needs its one read-only advisor review before chief_forge_init or chief_delegate. Not with workerThreadId.

tools.name: chief_roster
tools.description: Inspect this project's managed threads and their bounded persisted status, result, blocker, and recommendation. Opens with a Pending block naming each item's next action, in the same wording as its lifecycle alert. Add a todo with `todo.text` (and optional `after`, e.g. 'PR #42 merges'); change one by `todo.id`; close it with `state: done|dropped`. Track all Chief work here — including queued work nobody has delegated yet. Todos with an after: condition are summarised as one line; pass includeWaiting: true to list them. Each todo belongs to the Chief that added it; others' todos are listed apart and tagged — leave them unless the user asks.

includeWaiting.description: List todos that wait on an after: condition in full; by default the Pending block shows them as one count line.

tools.name: chief_inspect
tools.description: Inspect one managed thread's live status, persisted report summary, full-report file path, and bounded last assistant output before deciding what to do.

tools.name: chief_continue
tools.description: Send a short nudge (at most 500 characters) to a managed thread that is still working. Refused for any thread that has reported (ready or complete); follow-up work goes to a fresh worker, planner, reviewer, advisor or researcher (see the core rules).

instruction.description: A short nudge, at most 500 characters.

tools.name: chief_stop
tools.description: Interrupt a running managed thread that is stuck or looping. Keeps its worktree, branch, and history; the reply names the reroute steps.

reason.description: Why it is being stopped: what the evidence shows it stuck on.

tools.name: chief_review
tools.description: Only the active Chief starts reviews; the server refuses every other caller. Start or return an independent read-only review: for a worker with no plan link, in its existing worktree; for a plan worker, ONE review of the whole plan covering the latest worker of every branch, each pull request pinned to its own head commit. It is refused for an intermediate wave, a superseded worker, a design wave, and while any wave of the plan is not ready. With no worker, it reviews a pull request or branch in a fresh worktree; a branch a managed worker carries is refused (review that worker).

workerThreadId.description: An existing managed worker's thread id.

pullRequest.description: A pull request to review when no managed worker owns it: a number, an owner/repo#123 reference, or a PR URL. Resolved to its head branch with gh or glab, falling back to the raw value as a branch name.

branch.description: A branch to review when no managed worker owns it.

tools.name: chief_complete
tools.description: Mark an idle managed worker or reviewer complete after Chief has inspected sufficient evidence. Completing a worker also completes its reviewers and the advisors consulted on it, and — after the plan's final wave — its planner. A worker completed with an approving review (or a design wave with the owner's approval) while the cleanupApproved setting is on is then cleaned up by a background cleanup worker: it archives the task's threads when nothing else would be archived with them, deletes their bb/ worktree branches after bb removes the worktree and only when origin holds every commit, and clears their thread storage unless Chief's evidence is stored there; override and skipReview completions are never cleaned up. A design-only wave's worker completes only with the owner's approval recorded by chief_owner_approval. Any other worker with a pull request completes only when the newest review is an approve for the pull request's current head commit (a worker without one: for its current report); otherwise it is refused naming the reason. override (a reason) is the only bypass and is recorded in the result. skipReview (your reason) completes a worker without any review when you judge one unnecessary. A Spec Writer is never completed on any path (override and skipReview included), except on a test wave chief_skip_tests waived: its worker (or a tester rerun) follows it. After a worker completes, this call marks its draft pull request ready for review: never run gh pr ready or glab mr update --ready yourself for a worker's pull request.

override.description: Complete a worker even though no approve covers its pull request head (or current report). The reason is recorded in its result. Use only when the user or the evidence justifies skipping the review.

skipReview.description: Complete a worker without a review, by your own judgment: your reason, shown in chief_roster, chief_inspect and on the pull request. Refused only while a review of the task is running, without a ready report, on a design wave (needs chief_owner_approval), or together with override. Refused, like override, for a Spec Writer. Never cleaned up.

testsSkipped.description: Your reason for completing unplanned work with no tester: an unplanned worker whose task chain has no tester is refused without it. Shown in chief_roster, chief_inspect and on the pull request. A plan's test wave is waived with chief_skip_tests instead.

tools.name: chief_owner_approval
tools.description: Record the owner's approval of a design-only wave (a plan wave marked design: true). Only the owner approves design-only work; chief_review refuses it. Show the user the artboards from the designer's ready report, ask for explicit approval, then call this with their words verbatim. The wave that implements the artboards cannot be delegated, and the design wave cannot be completed, without it. A new report or chief_continue on the designer clears it. Refused for any other thread.

approval.description: The user's own words approving the artboards, verbatim.

tools.name: chief_skip_tests
tools.description: Go without a plan's test wave (test: true), by your own judgment: your reason is recorded on that wave and shown in chief_roster and chief_inspect. Before the wave is delegated, the wave drops out of the plan and its parent's worker ends the chain. After a tester ran on it, that tester stays the branch owner and you review or complete it (a blocked report counts). Refused while the wave's latest worker is running, once it is complete, or for a wave that is not a test wave. Calling it again changes nothing.

reason.description: Why this plan goes without that wave's tests.

tools.name: chief_skip_specs
tools.description: Go without the Spec Writer of a plan's spec: true implementation wave, by your own judgment, before that wave's first delegation: your reason is recorded on that wave (no Spec Writer can be delegated on it; its worker runs first and the review judges it against its plan) and shown in chief_roster, chief_inspect and the review. It never waives the tests. Refused for a wave that is not a spec: true implementation wave, or once any worker was delegated on it (re-plan with a fresh chief_plan instead). Calling it again changes nothing.

reason.description: Why this wave goes without its Spec Writer.

tools.name: chief_escalate
tools.description: Before you write a **Need you** request in chat, post it on the managed thread's pull request (else its tracking issue) with an @mention of the owner, so it is on record where the work is. threadId is the managed thread the request concerns; request is the full request. It returns at once; the post happens in the background. A planner with no tracking issue yet returns "chat only": then write the request in chat alone. Calling it again with the same request posts nothing new.

request.description: The full request, as you will write it in chat under Need you.

tools.name: chief_sync
tools.description: Fast-forward your own checkout to origin's default branch before you read code yourself. It never overwrites uncommitted or ignored files and never errors on a skip: it returns the old and new commit, or why it left the checkout as it is (a researcher or sharing planner is running, uncommitted changes, commits of its own, a failed fetch).

tools.name: chief_research
tools.description: Fan a read-only question out to parallel BB workflow agents. survey: answer `question` for each of `items` (files, symbols, topics), one verified row each with evidence. investigate: one agent per `questions` entry, then one merges the answers into a brief with Confirmed and Unconfirmed sections. Chief, planners and researchers may use survey and investigate. Reviewers, workers and advisors cannot use it. Read-only by prompt only: the agents share your checkout and permissions, and are told not to edit, commit, or push. From Chief the call returns at once with the id of a researcher thread that runs the research in your checkout and reports through chief_report; its report arrives as a lifecycle alert, so end your turn instead of polling. From a planner, each call waits up to the mode's timeout (10 minutes unless set in Chief researcher settings), and never more than 2.5 minutes, because some providers end tool calls at 3 minutes. If the run is still going it returns its runId: call chief_research again with the same mode and that runId to keep waiting; the run keeps going in between.

mode.description: survey: one row per item. investigate: one answer per sub-question, merged into a brief. Required unless resuming with runId.

question.description: The overall question or goal. Required unless resuming.

items.description: survey: files, symbols, or topics; each gets a row.

batchSize.description: survey: items per scan agent. Scan agents = ceil(items ÷ batchSize); aim for about 10 or fewer, since each runs concurrently and spends quota.

questions.description: investigate: sub-questions, one scan agent each.

verify.description: survey: add one agent that drops results it cannot confirm in the code.

models.description: Per-stage overrides: a full {provider, model, reasoningLevel} or nothing.

runId.description: Keep waiting on a run an earlier call started instead of starting a new one.
